activities.anchor: black swans existed in Australia all along the Europeans were
activities.caption: find the faulty line — induction's justification
activities.name: posInductionSpot

config.prompt: One line of this gloss on induction is wrong — click it:
lines: Every swan seen is white, therefore all swans are white — generalisation from observed to unobserved cases.
Deductive logic can license induction: the conclusion follows from the premises as stated.
Any attempt to justify induction inductively ("it has worked before") assumes the very principle it defends.
Goodman's grue — "green before 2100, blue after" — fits all observed emeralds just as truly as green does.
Science's warrant is self-correction: bold conjectures punished by experiment, replaced by better ones.
config.correction: Deductive logic cannot license it — the conclusion says more than the premises; that gap is Hume's problem, and no finite observations close it.
config.why: We are not owed induction's truth; we are owed a method that fails fast and locally — and science delivers that.

activities.anchor: starlight should bend by exactly 1.75 arc-seconds near the Sun
activities.caption: fill the blanks — Popper's asymmetry
activities.name: posDemarcCloze

config.text: A theory is scientific if it %%0%% some observable state of affairs — if it sticks its neck out. The asymmetry is the deep point: no number of confirmations %%1%% a universal law, but one genuine counter-instance %%2%% it.

activities.anchor: mistaking the everyday sense of theory (a hunch) for the scientific one
activities.caption: bet on the 2011 neutrino anomaly
activities.name: posCablePredict

config.q: 2011: neutrinos appear to travel faster than light. Why does no one declare relativity refuted the next morning?
choices: Duhem–Quine: the experiment tested a bundle — theory, instruments, auxiliaries — and the failing conjunct was a loose fibre-optic cable
A single counter-instance cannot refute a universal law
config.why: The faster-than-light anomaly turned out to be a loose fibre-optic cable — bundles fail one conjunct at a time.

activities.anchor: strict falsification would burn good theories regularly
activities.caption: file the research programmes — progressive or degenerating
activities.name: posLakatosSort

config.prompt: Lakatos's verdict, applied — file each programme:

items.label: a hard core protected from refutation plus an adjustable belt that keeps predicting novel facts — Neptune, gravitational lensing
adding epicycles can save anything, forever
adding Neptune saved Uranus's orbit — and told astronomers where to look
adjustments that merely explain what is already known

config.why: Demarcation, refined, is less a border fence than a quality assessment over time.

activities.anchor: Anomalies — stubborn misfits — accumulate at the edges
activities.caption: rebuild the Kuhn cycle
activities.name: posKuhnOrder

config.prompt: Rebuild the Kuhn cycle in order:
items: A paradigm takes hold — theory, methods, instruments and standards
Normal science: puzzle-solving within the paradigm
Anomalies — stubborn misfits — pile up at the edges
Heroic adjustments absorb them until they can't
Revolution: a new paradigm replaces the old, and textbooks are rewritten as if it had always been true
config.why: The Copernican replacement took a century of anomalies plus instruments — the telescope's Venus phases and Jupiter's moons — and a new exemplar.

activities.caption: drag the divider — prediction versus explanation
activities.name: posFlagpoleCompare

config.prompt: Drag the divider — why prediction and explanation come apart:

before.label: Prediction
before.text: From the shadow's length, the sun's angle and the laws of optics you can derive the flagpole's height — and machine-learning models predict brilliantly without explaining anything.

after.label: Explanation
after.text: From flagpole and sun you can explain the shadow: causation, mechanism, unification — the counterfactual account tells you how things would have differed had the cause differed.

config.why: Derivation runs both ways; explanation does not. "Explainable AI" is this gap with a funding line.

activities.anchor: by induction, today's will fail too
activities.caption: pair the realism debate's moves
activities.name: posRealismMatch

config.prompt: Realism versus anti-realism — pair each move with its content:

pairs.right: unobservables are approximately real — the best explanation of science's success (the "no miracles" argument)
believe the observable consequences, remain agnostic about the rest
phlogiston, caloric and the ether were successful and false — so success is poor evidence of truth
what survives theory change is structure — Fresnel's ether equations survive in modern optics

config.why: The debate stays open, sharpened by every unobservable that later turns out to be real — atoms, genes, neutrinos.

activities.anchor: The norms are aspirational, not descriptions
activities.caption: walk the eroding norms
activities.name: posMertonBranch

config.root: Merton's 1942 norms make science knowledge-producing as a community. Watch what eroding each one costs.

start.text: Pay-per-result incentives and secrecy arrive first. Which norms break?

choices.label: Disinterestedness and communalism
choices.feedback: The reward becomes payment per conclusion, and the shared pool that lets replication exist drains.

choices.label: Universalism
choices.feedback: Claims start being judged by who made them.

pay.text: Replication becomes a favour rather than a norm — much of the replication crisis is Duhem–Quine plus broken Mertonian norms.

celeb.text: Universalism erodes as celebrity and hierarchy rise; publish-or-perish attacks organised scepticism — every result must be new, negative results vanish.

config.why: Their erosion is measurable and consequential — the epistemology of science is partly design: which social machinery makes fallible humans self-correcting.
